chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 274: The Invisible Ghost – A Man Hangs Himself from Fear
chapter_meta_description: The invisible 'shrink-stealing ghost' drives a man to hang himself. Li Huowang must abandon his sword and seek out the County Magistrate to fight a threat he can't even see.
og_title: The Horror of the Invisible Ghost
og_description: Li Huowang faces a deadly curse he cannot stab. His only weapon is knowledge.
twitter_title: Ch. 274: Fear is the Real Killer
twitter_description: Li Huowang realizes the true enemy isn't a ghost—it's the town's collective fear.

lore_anchors.definition: A local administrative record of major events; an empty or sanitized gazetteer in the Dao-Twisted World signals official complicity or denial of supernatural horror.
A folk-horror entity believed to cause a man's penis (the 'life-root' or 命根子) to retract into his body. It is seen as an attack on a man's vital yang energy and his ability to reincarnate.
In Chinese folk belief, a term for the penis, viewed as a vital source of yang energy and a key to one's lineage and future reincarnation.
A classic Chinese philosophical and moral principle that judges a person by their actions rather than their private thoughts.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the waiter hang himself?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was terrified that the ghost would steal his "life-root," making his body incomplete and preventing his soul from reincarnating. He chose to die "whole" to escape an eternal torment as a restless ghost.
